fields.question: How can a feature add serving cost but no pipeline cost?
fields.answer: The model still pays embedding/projection work, but upstream generation/storage may already be paid by another model under that shared budget.
fields.example: If A already uses f, adding f to B leaves the shared union unchanged while B's inference FLOPs may rise.

fields.question: Why Pareto layers instead of a weighted task-FI sum?
fields.answer: Task losses differ in scale and units. Pareto layers retain features that cannot be dominated on all tasks before source blending chooses among them.
fields.example: For A(4,1), B(1,4), C(0,0), A/B share the first front and C is dominated.

fields.question: What differs from MLE Agents' variance-probe admission?
fields.answer: Fleet adds model resource caps and shared pipeline budgets. Better validation NE does not admit an infeasible candidate, and these caps do not replace same-round noise calibration.
fields.example: A candidate with NE0.1 but excessive inverse-QPS is rejected in favor of a feasible NE0.6 candidate.

fields.question: Why are rounding and cost order explicit inputs?
fields.answer: The fixed paper leaves those discrete conventions incomplete. Callers supply quotas, within-front order and real cost priorities; exhaustion or infeasibility is reported rather than silently padded.
fields.example: If two sources rank a first, the second skips a; source exhaustion is not silently refilled from elsewhere.

fields.question: Why is deeper cross-attention not already DNA?
fields.answer: A fixed-history stack reprojects S0 at every layer. DNA lets history absorb the newly updated request, so later layers read a changed S.
fields.example: The same history under two search queries may produce different S1; projecting fixed S0 cannot do this.

fields.question: Why does DNA-D have only D-1 history updates?
fields.answer: Both reads consume incoming S, and each update prepares the next layer. No read follows the final layer, so another update would not affect prediction.
fields.example: D3 reads S0, S1 and S2 and requires only two updates.

fields.question: How does it differ from LONGER?
fields.answer: LONGER concentrates history interaction into a smaller query/token path. DNA retains history tokens, updates them from a few request tokens and amortizes that work over candidates.
fields.example: Both can share K/V, but neither shared-K/V fact implies the same token-deletion schedule.

fields.question: Does within-request batching parity justify cross-request reuse?
fields.answer: No. A new U can change history states and invalidate prior S/KV. The local control covers only batch versus individual candidates using the same prepared request cache.
fields.example: Even with unchanged user history, a new search query requires new request-conditioned states.

fields.question: Does the10.3% online CTR lift validate LLM vectors?
fields.answer: No. LLM features were disabled in that experiment. It validates rules-to-learned retrieval and nearline serving; LLM incrementality is isolated offline only.
fields.example: BERT4Rec plus nearline beating rules does not prove that enabling LLM vectors adds a production lift.

fields.question: May a labeled click enter its own session input?
fields.answer: No. Event time must be strictly below the cutoff. Session and history split at session start and exclude the current label and future behavior.
fields.example: With cutoff10, events at10 and11 are both excluded; a less-than-or-equal check leaks the label.

fields.question: What does LSER add beyond YouTube DNN rather than generating recommendations with an LLM?
fields.answer: YouTube DNN aggregates history/context into a user tower. LSER separates short/long sequence encoders and adds optional LLM features plus asynchronous freshness. Both can query an offline item index; the LLM does not generate item IDs token by token.
fields.example: With LLM vectors disabled, LSER remains learned two-tower retrieval; this is the version used in its online A/B.

fields.question: Does a pending refresh call an LLM or invent zero vectors?
fields.answer: Neither. Select only records written by request time with admissible input cutoffs. Missing session/history explicitly requires external cold start; incomplete LLM pairs require compatible baseline fusion.
fields.example: At request10 a vector written_at12 is unavailable even with as_of9; this does not impose a paper-prescribed TTL.
